steps.title: Blocks, not grabs
steps.body: Linemen are there to ==protect the passer== and open running lanes. Holding lets a blocker win without being better, so the rule keeps blocking a ==fair fight==.

steps.title: Hands inside
steps.body: Blockers can push and steer with their ==hands inside the defender's frame==: the chest and the front of the shoulders. Grabbing and ==restricting== a player is holding.
steps.note: Ref signal: one hand grabbing the opposite wrist in front of the chest.

steps.title: The jersey grab
steps.body: The rusher beats the tackle to the outside, so the tackle ==grabs a fistful of jersey== and yanks him back. Flag.

steps.title: The takedown
steps.body: A rusher ==pulled to the ground== while getting past his blocker is the clearest hold there is. Refs almost always call it.

steps.title: Defensive holding
steps.body: Defenders can hold too. A cornerback who ==grabs a receiver== more than 5 yards past the line, before the ball is thrown, gets flagged.

steps.title: Ten yards back
steps.body: Offensive holding costs ==10 yards== and the down is replayed. Defensive holding is ==5 yards and an automatic first down==.

options: The tackle grabbed and pulled the rusher back
The quarterback held the ball too long
steps.explain: The rusher had the edge, so the tackle grabbed his jersey and hauled him back. That's offensive holding: 10 yards.
Offensive holding is 10 yards and the down is replayed. Defensive holding is 5 yards plus an automatic first down.
